prs.title: docs: point the READMEs at the 0.34.0 packages
prs.body:
## What

Moves every install snippet from 0.33.0 to 0.34.0, as #728 did for 0.33.0.

- `README.md`: the install table, the Swift package `from:`, the Gradle line
- `bindings/java/README.md`, `docs/desktop-java-csharp-distribution.md`: the Maven coordinate
- `bindings/python/docker/README.md`, `docs/python-distribution.md`: the service image tag in the pull, run, inspect, attestation and `SDK_VERSION` examples (the two move together; a guard in `offline-protocol-uniffi` compares them)
- `bindings/python/README.md`: the wheel build example
- `ProtocolEngine.cs`, `assemble-flutter-pub-package.sh`: the example version in a comment

Mentions that are historically correct ("available from 0.33.0", "not in 0.33.0 and earlier", the UPGRADING and SECURITY tables) are left alone.

## Merge order

**Merge only after the `v0.34.0` release run is green.** Until then these snippets name packages and an image that are not published.

## Testing

Docs and comments only. Not run locally; CI covers the image-tag guard.

prs.title: chore: release 0.34.0
prs.body:
Cuts 0.34.0: a minor, because the UDL gains the fast link API (#756).

## Version

Every file in the CONTRIBUTING "Cutting a Release" table moves to 0.34.0:
`Cargo.toml` (workspace version and the eleven internal dependencies), the five
local dependency versions in sealed, leaf and web, `Cargo.lock` and the two
tool lockfiles, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json` and its lockfile, `pubspec.yaml`,
and the three `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (regenerated). `SECURITY.md` supports
0.34.x.

## Prose

- **CHANGELOG:** `[0.34.0] — 2026-11-19` with a summary. Six merged PRs had no
  entry and now do: `forScenario` presets (#729), `mesh-sdk-doctor` (#734),
  `devTransportDiagnostics` (#736), the `parseProtocolEvent` helpers (#747), the
  browser Vite starter (#748), and both #752 fixes (the Python panic at
  interpreter exit, the one-line socket path error).
- **Archive:** 0.33.0 moves to `docs/changelog/0.33.md` and gains a row in both
  archive tables. The move is lossless: the section re-extracted from `main`
  with `](docs/` rewritten to `](../` is contained verbatim in the new file.
- **UPGRADING §32 (v0.34.0)**, plus the version index, platform table and the
  release summary paragraph:
  - Rust: `Event::FastLinkChanged` and `KeyPackagePayload.link_versions` break
    an exhaustive match or a full struct literal. TypeScript needs a
    `fast_link_changed` case, and a hand-written conformer of the generated
    engine interface needs six new methods.
  - A send beginning with `__FAST_LINK__` is refused with `InvalidArgument`.
  - `wifiDirect.fastLink` defaults to `'any'`: a React Native or Flutter app
    with Wi-Fi Direct on now hosts or joins a link a peer asks for, which on an
    iPhone with the Hotspot Configuration entitlement shows the system join
    prompt unasked.
  - The peer-stream window (64 KiB × 8), the new development console warnings,
    and one fewer storage write when the engine is dropped after `stop()`.

## Checks

- Every `](path#anchor)` in every tracked markdown file resolved on this branch
  and on `main`: the same 33 pre-existing failures on both, none added.
- `cargo deny check advisories` ok on `main` before the bump.

## Not in this PR

- Install pins (README, Java, Python, Docker, desktop docs, the C# doc comment)
  still say 0.33.0. They move in their own PR.
- #766 (WebRTC direct) and the open dependabot bumps.

After merge: a dispatch dry run or an rc tag, then `v0.34.0`.

prs.title: fix: close the gaps left after the compare sweep (#173 follow-up)
prs.body:
Follow-up to #173: the review fixes that didn't make it in before the merge, and the four things the nine-repo sweep showed were still missing.

## What changes

**Steps run as `runner`, as on GitHub** (`27438ed`)
- The built-in image gets a `runner` user with `/home/runner` and passwordless `sudo`. rustup and cargo live in its home; it owns what `pip install` and `npm install -g` write to.
- Steps exec into the job container as that user, with `USER` and `LOGNAME` set, when it can write the job's mounts. Otherwise (rootless engine, wrkflw run as root, a bare fallback image) they run as root with a warning. `WRKFLW_STEPS_AS_ROOT=1` keeps root everywhere.
- On Linux the user takes the uid of whoever runs wrkflw, so a bind-mounted workspace stays theirs. A workspace in a volume (macOS default) now gives copied-in files to uid 1001.
- `--dep-cache` mounts each cache in both root's home and the runner's.
- Unchanged: a job `container:`, an image mapped with `-P`, a step in its own container, Kubernetes, emulation.

**Opt-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for jobs** (`48e42ca`)
- `WRKFLW_JOB_GITHUB_TOKEN=1` fills `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` and `github.token` from `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, then `gh auth token`, where no provider gave one. Off by default, with a warning when on: it is the user's own token, not a run-scoped one.

**`compare` explains and counts honestly** (`e528aed`, `031f92f`)
- A job that failed only locally says which step, its exit code and the error line.
- The Docker note appears only when the output shows `docker` found no engine, not whenever an env var is unset.
- A Windows stand-in leg no longer switches off the run-level check; stand-in failures are left out of it instead.
- An agreeing job that passed a step whose action didn't run is marked `unverified` and counted in `unverified_agreements`.

**Review fixes from #173** (`3e6c5ac`)
- The `-gh` image tag now covers the install script, so changing the script rebuilds the layer.
- A composite action hands its environment on when a step returns an error, not only when it fails.
